top_stories.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as NVIDIA CEO, Trump claims credit amid controversy
points: NVIDIA's board voted unanimously to restore Jensen Huang as CEO and board member, effective immediately, after he had stepped away.
CFO Colette Kress had been juggling interim CEO duties alongside her finance role, an arrangement the board called unsustainable.
Huang co-founded NVIDIA over 30 years ago and has been its public face through every major milestone; founder reinstatements are rare at major tech companies.
Jensen Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee next week amid investigations into the reinstatement process.

unique_angles.point: Board conducted multiple meetings with Huang before voting, citing confidence in his transparency and vision for the AI 'industrial revolution.'

Trump personally called into the board meeting over a weekend, coordinated with VP Vance, and publicly took credit for the reversal, raising corruption concerns given his personal stake in NVIDIA stock; 54% of Americans believe the affair compromised national security, and some lawmakers have floated impeachment if improper influence is confirmed.

items.title: Why AI Gets Stuck on Age 34
points: When 65 different AI models generate random people with no extra instructions, 69 out of 100 invent someone exactly 34 years old.
The clustering happens because training data skews toward that demographic, so AI picks the statistical mode (most common value) instead of spreading across ages.
The same averaging effect appears with book recommendations: 73 out of 100 AIs suggest 'Man's Search for Meaning' with no reader context.
Adding personal details sharply reduces this clustering—personalized recommendations match the top generic suggestion only 4 out of 100 times, showing context makes AI responses more varied.

items.title: AI Detects Bladder Cancer Up to 5 Years Early
points: University of Plymouth AI analyzed records of nearly 70,000 patients, identifying 38 key warning signs out of 48,261 possible medical indicators.
The system correctly flags 85 out of 100 actual cancer cases and correctly clears 91 out of 100 patients without the disease.
It can spot warning signs up to 5 years before traditional diagnosis methods (blood-in-urine tests or camera scopes) catch it.
Researchers plan to test the system across other healthcare systems before clinical deployment, aiming to cut unnecessary invasive screenings.

items.title: Sutyo Cue Smart Glasses Remember Context From Conversations
points: The glasses listen to conversations and recall details—like a café a friend mentioned—without using a camera or screen.
Designed to help users follow through on casual promises made in conversation by surfacing remembered context later.

items.title: Anthropic Claims AI-Assisted Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
points: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis (a 167-year-old conjecture about hidden patterns in the gaps between prime numbers), including its generalized version.

The proof exists only as 17 million lines of Lean (a formal mathematics language resembling computer code) and was published only after Anthropic's IPO; Alpöge reportedly hadn't fully mastered the underlying math before release.

Lean and Mathlib communities express confidence in its correctness, but the Association for Human Mathematics warns AI-generated proofs shift accountability from humans and that Lean code is as fallible as any software.

Some researchers claim to have found bugs in the code and the proof remains unverified by traditional peer review; Terence Tao had claimed last month that AI labs secretly attempted and failed at Riemann, adding to skepticism about the timing.

items.title: SpaceX Pivots to Selling AI Compute Instead of Competing
points: Elon Musk told SpaceX employees the company is falling behind in AI and should focus on selling GPU compute to rivals like Anthropic rather than building competitive AI products.
An internal chat was renamed 'Sell Compute Because We Can't Compete,' and engineers were required to justify their GPU usage.
Musk shared data showing Grok (SpaceX's AI model) trailing significantly behind competitors, with no clear path forward for the company's own AI ambitions.
SpaceX is now functioning like a neocloud (a compute rental service) serving Anthropic's GPU demands rather than operating as a frontier AI lab.

items.title: Z.ai Previews GLM-5.4 Using Looped Transformer Architecture
points: GLM-5.4 uses looped transformers (an architecture where reasoning happens through repeated internal passes within the model's weights rather than visible steps), claiming to match a 2–3 trillion parameter model while using only 750 billion parameters.
The model introduces 'generalized coding,' writing code to solve problems directly—demonstrated by generating an entire music video in code instead of calling a separate video-generation model.
No benchmarks have been released yet, only a pre-release, prompting mixed reactions about whether this signals genuine efficiency gains or hidden weaknesses.

OpenAI and other major labs are reportedly embracing looped transformers despite reduced interpretability (the ability to see how a model reasons), with wider industry adoption expected within 3–4 months.

items.title: P=NP Emerges as Next AI Math Target
points: With the Riemann hypothesis reportedly addressed, P=NP (the question of whether problems that are easy to verify are also easy to solve) is being called the 'final boss' of unsolved mathematics.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI have published limited P=NP proofs exploring algebraic approaches, suggesting this is the next frontier for AI-assisted mathematical discovery.

issues.subject: AI Just Made History in the Middle of a Meltdown

headlines: Anthropic mathematician claims to have proven the Riemann hypothesis using Claude AI, releasing proof as 17 million lines of Lean code—the approach is unprecedented and raises questions about human understanding and verification of AI-generated mathematics.

Elon Musk told SpaceX employees the company is falling behind in AI and should focus on selling compute to rivals like Anthropic rather than building competitive products, with internal chat renamed 'Sell Compute Because We Can't Compete.'

Trump personally intervened in Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia, calling the board and coordinating with VP Vance—transforming a corporate governance scandal into a potential corruption issue as Jensen faces Senate testimony next week.

Chinese AI lab Z.ai previewed GLM-5.4 using looped transformers (internal reasoning loops that reduce visible computation), claiming to match a much larger model with far fewer parameters, sparking industry debate over inference efficiency versus explainability.

Skepticism over the Riemann proof is growing as some claim bugs exist in the Lean code, verification remains incomplete, and critics argue the approach sidesteps human mathematical understanding entirely.

sections.title: 1. The Riemann Hypothesis "Proof" and Its Controversy
points: Levent Alpöge at Anthropic claims he and Claude proved that the Riemann hypothesis—a 167-year-old conjecture stating that gaps between prime numbers follow a hidden pattern—is true, and that the method extends to the generalized version.

The proof exists only as 17 million lines of Lean (a formal mathematics language that acts like computer code), was published only after Anthropic's IPO, and Alpöge had not fully mastered the underlying mathematics himself before release.

Lean and Mathlib communities express confidence the proof is correct, but the Association for Human Mathematics warns that AI-generated proofs shift accountability away from humans and that Lean proofs are as fallible as any software program.

Some researchers claim to have found bugs in the code, and the proof remains unverified by traditional peer review; treating it as "rock solid" is premature, though experts note the approach represents something genuinely new in how mathematics can be conducted.

sections.title: 2. Trump's Intervention in Jensen Huang's Reinstatement
points: Trump personally called into the Nvidia board meeting over a weekend, coordinated with VP Vance, and told CNBC the reinstatement would not have happened without his involvement—publicly claiming credit for reversing the board's earlier decision to remove Huang.

Trump's overt involvement transforms the scandal from corporate governance into potential corruption, especially as the president personally benefits from Nvidia stock and 54% of Americans believe the affair compromised national security.

Jensen Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee next week; Congressional Democrats and Republican national security leaders have signaled wide-ranging investigations, with some suggesting impeachment grounds if improper influence is proven.

Tech leaders celebrated the reinstatement, while critics outside the industry expressed serious skepticism—Stephanie Ruhle challenged the "obvious innocence" framing given Trump's financial stake in Nvidia's stock performance.

sections.title: 3. SpaceX's AI Failure and the Compute-Selling Pivot
points: Elon Musk told SpaceX engineers the company is falling behind in AI and explicitly instructed staff to prioritize selling GPU compute to rivals (especially Anthropic) over using it for internal products, renaming an internal chat 'Sell Compute Because We Can't Compete.'

Musk shared performance data showing Grok (SpaceX's AI model) trailing significantly, required engineers to justify GPU usage, indicating a dysfunctional AI effort with no clear path forward for the company's own AI capabilities.

SpaceX is functionally operating as a neocloud (compute rental service) for Anthropic's intensive GPU demands rather than as a frontier AI lab, marking a dramatic reversal from Musk's earlier ambitions to compete in AI development.

sections.title: 4. Z.ai's GLM-5.4 and the "Looper" Architecture Debate
points: GLM-5.4 uses looped transformers (a architecture where reasoning happens inside the model's weights through repeated internal passes rather than visible steps), claiming to match a 2–3 trillion parameter model using only 750 billion parameters and cheaper inference.

The model introduces "generalized coding" where the AI writes code to solve problems directly—demonstrated by generating an entire music video in code rather than calling a separate video generation model—blurring boundaries between reasoning and tool use.

No benchmarks have been released yet (only a pre-release), which some read as a warning sign while others view it as the beginning of a broader industry shift toward looped transformers for efficiency gains.

OpenAI and other major labs are embracing looped transformers despite sacrificing interpretability (the ability to see how the model is reasoning), suggesting this approach will become standard within 3–4 months as labs scale to 2–3 trillion parameters.

sections.title: 5. The Broader AI Narrative Fracture
points: The Anthropic IPO is increasingly cast as a cynical liquidity grab following the Riemann hypothesis announcement, raising questions about motivations for publishing an unverified proof immediately after going public.

Terence Tao claimed last month that AI labs secretly attempted Riemann and failed, making the sudden success claim suspicious to some observers; Tao had predicted a fundamentally new type of mathematics would be needed to solve it.

The convergence of Jensen's scandal, Musk's compute-selling admission, unverified mathematical claims, and architectural shifts toward less-transparent reasoning suggests the AI industry's credibility is fragmenting under scrutiny.

sections.title: P=NP Problem Now in Focus
points: With the Riemann hypothesis reportedly solved, P=NP (the question of whether certain hard-to-verify problems can be solved as easily as they can be checked) is emerging as "the final boss" of unsolved mathematics that AI may target next.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI have published limited P=NP proofs exploring algebraic space, suggesting this problem is the next frontier for AI-assisted mathematical discovery.
